mainTopic: Which rules are on the list of ways a גט and a שטר שחרור are alike, and why a כותי witness is accepted on a גט
overview: The גמרא first explains that even the תנא קמא can hold like רבי אלעזר. He differs from רבי שמעון only when the gentile witnesses have clearly gentile names (שמות מובהקין). Next, the גמרא settles which rules go on the list of ways a גט and a שטר שחרור are alike: only rules that do not also apply to קידושין. חזרה fits this rule because it is about שליחות against the recipient's will, which works for divorce but not for betrothal. A new משנה then teaches that a document signed by a כותי witness is invalid, except for a גט and a שטר שחרור, and tells how רבן גמליאל accepted a גט with כותי witnesses. The גמרא asks whose view this is, and quotes a ברייתא with three views on a כותי's מצה. It shows that none of the three seems to explain why a גט is different. It tries to fit the משנה to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and rejects that, because only one כותי witness is allowed. Finally it says the משנה follows רבי אלעזר and speaks of a case where a Jew signed last. The explanation of that case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The real disagreement is about clearly gentile names
steps.stepSummary: Even the תנא קמא can agree with רבי אלעזר. He and רבי שמעון disagree only about a גט signed by witnesses whose names are clearly gentile.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the case of clearly gentile names.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers how the תנא קמא can hold like רבי אלעזר and still argue with רבי שמעון. Their argument is narrowed to one case: signatures with clearly gentile names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that the witnesses who watch the גט being handed over are the ones who make it work (עדי מסירה כרתי). The תנא קמא worries that the handing-over might have happened in front of those same gentiles, so he says the גט is invalid מדרבנן. רבי שמעון says that when the names are clearly gentile, we can assume it was handed over in front of valid witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
The witnesses to the handing-over are what make the divorce work (רבי אלעזר's view)

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
in the case of clearly gentile names.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of how the תנא קמא could hold like רבי אלעזר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the disagreement to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the תנא קמא must hold like רבי מאיר that the signing witnesses make the divorce work, so a gentile-signed גט would be invalid מדאורייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא can hold like רבי אלעזר. His ruling of invalid is only a rabbinic concern, and the argument with רבי שמעון is about שמות מובהקין.

steps.title: But retraction is a Torah rule, and it is on the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the list leaves out Torah-level rules. חזרה, cancelling the שליחות, is Torah law, and yet the ברייתא lists it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But retraction is a Torah law, and it is taught in the list!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier explanation for why gentile witnesses are left off the list of ways a גט and a שטר שחרור are alike. That explanation said the list leaves out Torah-level rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, a husband or master can take back his instruction to his שליח, and this is Torah law. Yet the list includes it. So the line 'the list leaves out Torah-level rules' cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Retraction: taking back the instruction before the document is delivered

phrases.english: But retraction is from the Torah, and yet it teaches it!
phrases.notes: This means the husband or master can cancel the שליח's job before the document is handed over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule behind the list, now that gentile witnesses have been shown to be possibly rabbinic
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the list leaves out Torah-level rules
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah-level rule, חזרה, appears on the list, so 'Torah vs. rabbinic' cannot be what decides inclusion.

steps.title: New rule: the list only includes things that don't apply to betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier approach. The list includes only rules that do not also apply to קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches only a matter that does not exist in betrothal. A matter that does exist in betrothal, it does not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up its old explanation and offers a brand-new reason for what goes on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is now whether the rule is special to גיטין and שחרורים. A rule that also applies to קידושין is left off.
steps.confusionAlert: אֶלָּא here means the גמרא is replacing its earlier explanation entirely, not adding to it.

phrases.english: Rather, when it teaches,
it teaches a matter that does not exist in betrothal;
a matter that does exist in betrothal,
it does not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 2 knocked down
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list was thought to leave out Torah-level rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list includes only rules that do not also apply to קידושין.

steps.title: But retraction also applies to betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new rule. חזרה itself also applies to קידושין, so why is it on the list?
steps.simpleTranslation: But retraction itself exists in betrothal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new rule against the same example, חזרה. Someone who sends a שליח to do קידושין can also cancel it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the list includes only rules that don't apply to קידושין, then חזרה should not be on it. So the new rule seems to fail as well.

phrases.english: But retraction itself
exists in betrothal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new rule from step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the list includes only things that don't apply to קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חזרה is on the list, but it also applies to קידושין.

steps.title: The case is agency against her will, which works only for divorce
steps.stepSummary: The חזרה on the list is about a שליח sent against the recipient's will. That kind of שליחות works for גירושין but not for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to agency against her will, which exists in divorce but does not exist in betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves the new rule. The kind of שליחות discussed on the list is one that exists only in divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט can be given to a woman without her consent, so a שליח can be sent to divorce her against her will. קידושין needs her consent, so that kind of שליחות does not exist there. The case on the list is therefore special to גירושין, and the rule from step 3 holds.
steps.whatToRemember: The list of ways a גט and a שטר שחרור are alike includes only rules that do not apply to קידושין. The חזרה on the list fits because it is about שליחות against the recipient's will, which works only for divorce.

phrases.english: It refers to agency against her will,
which exists in divorce
but does not exist in betrothal.
phrases.notes: A woman can be divorced without agreeing, but she can't be betrothed without agreeing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 and keeps the rule from step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזרה seemed to apply equally to קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case on the list is שליחות against the recipient's will, which exists only in גירושין.

steps.title: A document with a Samaritan witness is invalid, with two exceptions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that any document signed by a כותי witness is invalid, except a גט for a woman and a שטר שחרור for a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any document that has a כותי witness signed on it is invalid, except for a woman's גט and a document that frees a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a general rule about documents signed by a כותי witness, plus two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that a כותי cannot serve as a witness on a document. The משנה carves out two exceptions: a גט and a שטר שחרור. For these two, a כותי witness does not disqualify the document.

keyTerms.meaning: a Samaritan, a member of a group whose status as Jews was in doubt

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גט means any legal document, not only a divorce. That is why the משנה can list גיטי נשים, divorces, as an exception.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Any document
phrases.notes: In this line גט means any legal document, not just a divorce.

phrases.english: that has a Samaritan witness on it is invalid,
except for women's bills of divorce
and documents freeing slaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל גֵּט שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו עֵד כּוּתִי – פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It does not continue the earlier discussion about the list of rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כותי witness invalidates a document, except for a גט and a שטר שחרור.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל approved a divorce with Samaritan witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells a story: a גט signed by כותי witnesses came before רבן גמליאל in כפר עותנאי, and he ruled it valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case where they brought a woman's גט before רבן גמליאל in the village of כפר עותנאי. Its witnesses were כותים, and he ruled it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up its exception for a גט with a real case decided by רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that the exception for a גט was actually applied in practice. A גט signed only by כותי witnesses was accepted as valid.

keyTerms.meaning: an actual incident, told as support for a ruling

phrases.english: An incident in which they brought before Rabban Gamliel
in the village of Otnai a woman's bill of divorce,
and its witnesses were Samaritan witnesses,
and he declared it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the exception for a גט from step 6 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a גט signed by כותי witnesses is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: A case decided by רבן גמליאל in כפר עותנאי

steps.title: No known opinion seems to fit the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows, and claims it matches none of the three תנאים in a ברייתא it is about to quote.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה? It is not the תנא קמא, not רבי אלעזר, and not רבן שמעון בן גמליאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge: the משנה does not seem to match any of three known opinions. This sets up the ברייתא quoted in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Although it is worded as a question, this is really a problem. Every opinion we know about כותים seems to lead to a different result than the משנה. The גמרא will now show where those three opinions come from.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Whose opinion is our Mishna?

phrases.aramaic: לָא תַּנָּא קַמָּא, וְלָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Not the first Tanna, and not Rabbi Elazar,
and not Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which תנא the משנה from step 6 follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a כותי witness is valid only on a גט and a שטר שחרור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each known opinion on the status of כותים would lead to a different result than the משנה.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a כותי's מצה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives three views on a כותי's מצה. The תנא קמא permits it. רבי אלעזר forbids it because כותים are not expert in the details of מצוות‎. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says they are extra careful with any מצוה they took on.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: a כותי's מצה is permitted, and a person can fulfill his obligation on פסח with it. רבי אלעזר forbids it, because they are not expert in the fine details of מצוות‎. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: any מצוה the כותים took upon themselves, they are very careful with, more than Jews are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source of the three opinions it mentioned. This is background for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each view takes a different stance on how much we can trust כותים. The תנא קמא trusts them fully. רבי אלעזר does not trust them on details. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trusts them only with the מצוות they accepted, and with those, fully.

phrases.english: As it is taught: The matza of a Samaritan is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: and a person fulfills his obligation with it on Pesach.
Rabbi Elazar forbids it,
because they are not expert in the fine details of מצוות.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Any מצוה that the Samaritans took upon themselves,
they are very careful with it, more than Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source of the three opinions named in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three views on a כותי's מצה: permitted (תנא קמא), forbidden (רבי אלעזר), and trusted for מצוות they accepted (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל).

steps.title: Neither the תנא קמא nor רבי אלעזר fits
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה followed the תנא קמא, other documents should also be valid. If it followed רבי אלעזר, even a גט should be invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? If it is the תנא קמא, then even other documents should be valid too! If it is רבי אלעזר, then not even a woman's גט should be valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its challenge. It shows why the משנה cannot follow the תנא קמא or רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא treats כותים like Jews, so they should be able to sign any document, not just a גט. רבי אלעזר does not trust them, so they should not be able to sign even a גט. The משנה takes a middle path that neither view explains. The next step shows the problem with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: Whose is it? If the first Tanna,
then even other documents should be valid too!
If Rabbi Elazar,
then not even a woman's divorce should be valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִי תַּנָּא קַמָּא, אֲפִילּוּ שְׁאָר שְׁטָרוֹת נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 9 to spell out the challenge raised in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the משנה follows the תנא קמא or רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תנא קמא would accept a כותי on every document. רבי אלעזר would accept a כותי on none. The משנה accepts a כותי only on a גט and a שטר שחרור.

steps.title: The משנה does not fit רבן שמעון בן גמליאל either
steps.stepSummary: The third leg of the challenge: by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule, a כותי is either reliable for all documents or for none, so the משנה's split does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: if the כותים took on this מצוה, then even other documents should be valid; if they did not take it on, then even a גט for a woman should not be valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge from step 10 by testing the third view, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and showing it does not fit the משנה either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said כותים are careful only with מצוות they took on. So the only question is whether they took it on. Either answer gives one rule for all documents, but the משנה splits: a גט is valid, other documents are not.

keyTerms.meaning: They took on (a מצוה) and hold onto it firmly
Other documents (like loan or sale documents)
A bill of divorce given to a woman

steps.whatToRemember: All three views in the ברייתא give one rule for every document, so none of them explains why the משנה makes a גט different.

phrases.english: And if it is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel;
if they took it on firmly –
phrases.notes: He means: if the כותים accepted this מצוה as their own, like he said about מצה.

phrases.english: then even other documents too should be valid,
if they did not take it on –
then even a woman's גט should not be valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the three-way challenge begun in step 10 by testing the last view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His rule depends only on whether כותים accepted the מצוה, which leads to one rule for all documents, but the משנה splits between a גט and other documents.

steps.title: Suggestion: they took on גיטין but not other documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה could follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל after all: the כותים took on the laws of גיטין, but not the laws of other documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say it is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and they took on this one (גיטין) but did not take on that one (other documents)...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer: maybe the כותים are careful about גיטין but not about other documents. This sets up a challenge that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer would explain the split in the משנה: a גט is valid because כותים took on the laws of גיטין, and other documents are not valid because they did not take on those laws. The words 'וְכִי תֵּימָא' warn us that the גמרא is about to knock this answer down.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggested answer, usually about to be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer is not the גמרא's final view. 'וְכִי תֵּימָא' introduces a suggestion that the גמרא will reject in the next line.

phrases.english: And if you will say
it is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and they took on this one
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the מצוה of גיטין.

phrases.english: and did not take on that one,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the laws of other documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer step 11's challenge by splitting which מצוות the כותים accepted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: they accepted גיטין but not other documents.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל cannot explain why only a גט is valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: He can, if the כותים took on גיטין but not the laws of other documents.

steps.title: Then why only one כותי witness?
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected: if כותים were trusted with גיטין, two כותי witnesses should work too, yet רבי אלעזר said only one כותי witness is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why only one? Even two should be fine! Why then did רבי אלעזר say: They only allowed one כותי witness on it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 12 by pointing to a ruling that only one כותי witness may sign a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If כותים really took on the laws of גיטין, they would be fully trusted, and a גט with two כותי witnesses would be fine. But רבי אלעזר limited it to one כותי witness, so the כותים are not fully trusted, and the answer from step 12 cannot be right.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבי אלעזר quoted here, who said only one כותי witness is allowed, is a later אמורא. He is not the same person as the תנא רבי אלעזר in the ברייתא about מצה.

phrases.english: If so,
why specifically one?
phrases.notes: He means one כותי witness on the גט.

phrases.english: Even two should also be fine!
Why then did Rabbi Elazar say:
They did not make it valid
except with just one כותי witness?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the suggestion of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole idea that the משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Full trust in כותים for גיטין would allow two כותי witnesses, but the ruling allows only one.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי אלעזר: a Jew signed last
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's real answer: the משנה follows רבי אלעזר, who does not trust כותים, and it speaks about a case where a Jewish witness signed after the כותי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is רבי אלעזר, and the case is where a Jew signed last.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer: the משנה follows רבי אלעזר, and it starts to describe the special case it is talking about. The explanation of why that case helps continues after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר does not trust כותים, so in general a כותי's signature does not count. The משנה is about a special case where a Jewish witness signed below the כותי. The גמרא is about to explain why that makes a גט valid but not other documents.

keyTerms.meaning: And for example, the case is where

phrases.english: Really, it is Rabbi Elazar,
and the case is where a Jew signed last,

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, וּכְגוֹן דְּחָתֵים יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the גמרא goes back to רבי אלעזר, which step 10 had challenged, and answers that challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the משנה speaks about a specific way the גט was signed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By רבי אלעזר even a גט signed by a כותי should be invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a גט where a Jewish witness signed after the כותי. The explanation continues after this line.
